now.text: Fix pushed as PR #12885 (branch worktree-agent-ad4ea9c1b8378833d). Criteria 0-4 stamped with mutation proofs; criterion 5 is merge-gated and reserved for the lead — do not stamp it from here. Awaiting required checks: Cloud gate, Console gate, Elixir gate, PR references an active task (already PASS), plus go vet + test.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The tripwire's walk is scoped to the module's own TRACKED sources so nested agent checkouts cannot be mistaken for the module. Evidence quotes the clean-tree run: PASS plus the runtime, against the 161.4s FAIL measured before.
acceptance_criteria.evidence:
SCOPED via `git ls-files -z -- '*.go'` rooted at the module root, replacing `exec.Command("grep","-rn","--include=*.go",<pat>,".")`. Domain measured at the primary checkout: 767 tracked .go files versus 228 on-disk copies of joincols.go (227 of them under gitignored .claude/worktrees/ and .omx/).

BEFORE (primary checkout, /Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark):
  FAIL github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/internal/pdrender  161.432s
  ...227 lines of ./.claude/worktrees/*/internal/pdrender/joincols.go:33 and ./.omx/*/...

AFTER (this worktree, clean tree):
  === RUN   TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver
  --- PASS: TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver (0.15s)
  ok  github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/internal/pdrender  0.322s

Full package suite also green: `go test ./internal/pdrender/` -> ok 0.583s. 161.4s -> 0.15s on the tripwire, and the walk can no longer see a nested checkout.

Note on how this was verified: this worktree contains only 1 copy of joincols.go, so a local PASS here is by itself vacuous — it would have passed even unfixed. The 161.4s FAIL above was therefore reproduced at the primary checkout, which is where the 228 copies live.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: MUTATION ARM A — a divide-formula violation planted in an EXISTING tracked .go file reds the test, and the evidence quotes the failure naming that file:line. A guard is proven by making it fail, not by watching it pass.
acceptance_criteria.evidence:
MUTATION ARM A — PROVEN. Planted a genuine divide-formula violation at the end of internal/pdrender/attrs.go, an EXISTING tracked file that the fix's git ls-files enumeration covers:

  func mutationProbeAlpha(avail, tracks, gutter int) int {
      cellW := (avail - (tracks-1)*gutter) / tracks
      return cellW
  }

`go test ./internal/pdrender/ -run TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver`:

  --- FAIL: TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver (0.14s)
      joincols_test.go:248: inline divide-formula copies remain outside the joincols solver:
          internal/pdrender/attrs.go:140:cellW := (avail - (tracks-1)*gutter) / tracks
  FAIL github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/internal/pdrender  0.310s

The guard fired, named the exact file:line:content, and did so in 0.14s. Reverted via `git checkout -- internal/pdrender/attrs.go`; the tree is clean of the probe and the suite is green again (ok 0.583s). This is the arm that proves the fix narrowed the DOMAIN without weakening the ASSERTION.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: MUTATION ARM B — a violation in a NEWLY ADDED tracked .go file (a fresh renderer, the realistic regression) also reds it. This is the arm that a tracked-only scope could plausibly have broken, so it is proven separately rather than assumed from arm A.
acceptance_criteria.evidence:
MUTATION ARM B — PROVEN. This arm exists because the fix's scope change is exactly the kind that could silently stop catching NEW files: git ls-files reports tracked paths, so an untracked scratch file is invisible to it. A fresh renderer arriving as a new file is the realistic regression, so it was tested separately rather than inferred from arm A.

Created internal/pdrender/mutation_probe.go and `git add`ed it (staged files ARE reported by git ls-files):

  package pdrender

  func mutationProbeBeta(avail, tracks, Gutter int) int {
      cellW := (avail - (tracks-1)*Gutter) / tracks
      return cellW
  }

`go test ./internal/pdrender/ -run TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver`:

  --- FAIL: TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver (0.13s)
      joincols_test.go:248: inline divide-formula copies remain outside the joincols solver:
          internal/pdrender/mutation_probe.go:4:cellW := (avail - (tracks-1)*Gutter) / tracks
  FAIL github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/internal/pdrender  0.309s

Note this probe used the capital-G `Gutter` spelling, exercising the regex's [Gg] class on a different branch than arm A. Probe removed with `git rm -f`; `git status --short` shows only the intended joincols_test.go modification.

DISCLOSED LIMITATION, since it is a real narrowing and should not be discovered later by someone else: a violation in a file that is neither tracked nor staged is NOT scanned. That is the intended domain — a real violation reaches main as committed code, and both committed and staged states are covered — but it does mean the guard no longer reds on a purely local untracked scratch file the way the old repo-wide walk did.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The liveness self-check survives: zero allowlisted hits in the solver still hard-fails, so a pattern that drifts away from the code cannot leave a silently vacuous guard. Enumerating zero files likewise reds rather than passing empty.
acceptance_criteria.evidence:
LIVENESS SELF-CHECK — PROVEN BY MUTATION, not by reading the diff. The `ownerSeen` fatal is the arm that stops the tripwire from going quietly vacuous if the pattern ever drifts away from the code it polices, so it was made to fire.

Temporarily drifted the pattern so it can no longer match the solver:

  pattern := regexp.MustCompile(`cellWZZZ *:=.*[Gg]utter`)

`go test ./internal/pdrender/ -run TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver`:

  --- FAIL: TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver (0.14s)
      joincols_test.go:245: divide-formula pattern matched nothing in the joincols solver — the tripwire regex has drifted and guards nothing
  FAIL github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/internal/pdrender  0.357s

It hard-failed on the drift rather than reporting a clean tree. Restored from a byte-level backup; `grep -n MustCompile` confirms line 218 is back to `cellW *:=.*[Gg]utter` and the suite is green (ok 0.583s).

The two other vacuity paths are also closed by construction and are new in this fix: `git ls-files` returning zero .go files t.Fatals ("would pass vacuously") instead of scanning an empty set, and a tracked file that cannot be read t.Fatals rather than being skipped. The old code had an equivalent guard only for grep's exit status, which is the one this fix removed the need for.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The guard no longer depends on grep semantics at all, so the documented ugrep-wrapper-vs-GNU-grep divergence on ignored paths can no longer make it behave one way locally and another in CI. Evidence names the mechanism that replaced it.
acceptance_criteria.evidence:
GREP DEPENDENCY REMOVED — and the divergence it exposed the guard to was MEASURED, not assumed, because it is far larger than expected and it points the wrong way.

At the primary checkout, same pattern, same root, same flags:

  shell `grep -rn --include=*.go 'cellW *:=.*[Gg]utter' .`      ->    5 matches
  /usr/bin/grep -rn --include=*.go 'cellW *:=.*[Gg]utter' .     ->  228 matches

A 45x disagreement. `type grep` shows the shell name is a function that execs `ugrep -G --ignore-files --hidden -I --exclude-dir=.git ...`, so it honours .gitignore and never sees .claude/worktrees/ or .omx/. Go's `exec.Command("grep", ...)` performs no shell function lookup — it resolves the real binary from PATH, which walks everything.

This inverts the usual host trap. The instrument a human reaches for to investigate this bug (typing grep) reports 5 and looks healthy; the instrument the failing test actually used reports 228. Anyone who had debugged the red by hand-running the guard's own command would have concluded there was nothing wrong. That is also why a fix that merely added exclude flags to the grep call would have been unverifiable locally — it would behave one way under the wrapper and another under CI's GNU grep.

The fix removes the dependency rather than tuning it: enumeration via `git ls-files` (one documented ignore semantics, the same one git itself uses) and matching via Go's `regexp` package, which is the same RE2 engine on every host and in CI. The pattern `cellW *:=.*[Gg]utter` carries over unchanged — POSIX BRE and RE2 agree on `*`, `.*` and `[Gg]` — so the assertion is byte-identical while the instrument is now host-invariant.

MEASURED 2026-08-20. go test ./internal/pdrender/ fails in any working copy that carries agent worktrees, and the failure is the guard looking at reflections of itself.

TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver (internal/pdrender/joincols_test.go) shelled out to grep -rn --include=*.go "cellW *:=.*[Gg]utter" . with cmd.Dir set to the module root found by go.mod walk-up. That . is the whole repo, and this repo hosts a full checkout per agent under .claude/worktrees/ plus .omx/. Measured at the primary checkout: find . -name joincols.go returns 228 copies against 1 tracked by git. The tripwire matched its own pattern in 227 copies of itself and failed after 161.4s.

SCOPE — THIS IS LOCAL-ONLY, NOT A BROKEN MAIN. go-tests.yml on branch main is SUCCESS on its recent runs. .claude/worktrees/ is gitignored (.gitignore:118), so a fresh actions/checkout has no nested trees and CI never sees the condition. The cost is a false regression for every local dev plus a ~2.5-minute test, not an outage — filed at that priority. The real damage is to the guard: a tripwire that reliably cries wolf locally is one people learn to ignore, and this one could no longer tell a genuine violation from an echo of itself.

THE HOST TRAP, WHICH INVERTS THE USUAL ONE. On this machine an interactive grep is a ugrep wrapper carrying --ignore-files, but exec.Command("grep", ...) resolves the REAL grep from PATH. So the Go test saw gitignored paths that a human typing the same grep in the same directory would NOT — the two instruments disagree about exactly the paths that cause this bug. Any fix that keeps a grep dependency has to be verified under both. The fix taken here removes the dependency instead: enumerate via git ls-files and match in-process with Go's regexp, which is the same engine everywhere.

WHAT MUST NOT WEAKEN. The assertion is unchanged — no .go file outside the joincols solver may re-inline the per-cell divide-formula. Narrowing the DOMAIN to tracked sources is correct (a real violation arrives as committed code) but it must still fire, including on a newly added renderer. Both arms are proven by mutation below, not by reading.
